summary: This study investigates how enhancer pairs combine to regulate promoters in mouse embryonic stem cells using a large-scale three-way combinatorial MPRA. Results show that enhancer pairs generally combine near-additively across seven developmental promoters, with promoter strength influencing non-linear signal scaling. Weaker promoters exhibit supra-additivity, indicating context-dependent integration. A housekeeping promoter shows a distinct, more limited response. The findings support additive enhancer integration with promoter-mediated non-linear transformation, advancing understanding of gene regulation complexity.

notes.why_it_supports: This directly supports the central finding that additive integration is the predominant mode of enhancer-enhancer interaction in mammalian genomes.
